title: Internal: handling procedure for a past-due Club Membership contract settling up and cancelling
content:
## Scope
This document covers the internal procedure for a Club Membership contract that is currently in past due standing, whose member has decided, on settling up, to cancel rather than continue.

## Applicable situation
This procedure applies to a membership contract currently sitting in past due standing whose member wishes to settle the missed payment and then give notice of cancellation. It reconciles the missed payment that caused the past-due standing, brings the contract back to active standing, records the member's own notice of cancellation, and, since the member remains within their tier's own minimum committed term, assesses the corresponding early-termination fee. Once complete, the contract is current on its billing history, back in active standing, carries a pending cancellation request awaiting its own notice period, and has been billed the early-termination fee due at the moment notice was given.

## Steps, in order
1. The representative posts the late fee for the missed payment that caused the past-due standing, by calling charge_late_fee_8963437d.
2. The representative collects the reactivation payment, by calling pay_reactivation_balance_4f725d24.
3. The representative brings the contract back to active standing, by calling reactivate_membership_73e153df.
4. The customer themselves files their own notice of cancellation, by calling file_cancellation_notice_df814962.
5. The representative posts the early-termination fee, by calling charge_early_termination_fee_74e8dbe7.

## Role table
| Step | Tool | Performed by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | charge_late_fee_8963437d | the representative |
| 2 | pay_reactivation_balance_4f725d24 | the representative |
| 3 | reactivate_membership_73e153df | the representative |
| 4 | file_cancellation_notice_df814962 | the customer themselves |
| 5 | charge_early_termination_fee_74e8dbe7 | the representative |

## Ordering rationale
Step 1 must precede step 2 because the reactivation payment amount is computed from the contract's current dues balance, and posting the late fee changes that balance; posting the late fee after the reactivation payment would collect an amount that omits the very fee the member owes, permanently understating what was collected. Step 2 must precede step 3 because bringing the contract back to active standing is only warranted once the outstanding balance driving the past-due standing has actually been paid down; reactivating first would return the contract to active standing while still owing the settlement amount. Step 3 must precede step 4 because a cancellation notice may only be filed from active or frozen standing, never from past due standing; filing notice before reactivation would attempt a transition the contract's own lifecycle does not define. Step 4 must precede step 5 because the early-termination fee is anchored on the moment notice of cancellation is given and requires the member to no longer be in past-due standing; assessing the fee before notice exists would bill a charge for an event that has not yet occurred.

## What would be missing if two adjacent steps were swapped
Swapping steps 1 and 2 would compute the reactivation payment before the late fee is on the books, so the amount collected would fall short of what the member actually owes. Swapping steps 2 and 3 would bring the contract back to active standing while an outstanding balance still remains unpaid. Swapping steps 3 and 4 would attempt to file a cancellation notice while the contract is still in past-due standing, which its own lifecycle does not permit. Swapping steps 4 and 5 would attempt to assess the early-termination fee before any cancellation notice exists to anchor it to.
